_comment: Module 4 (electricity). Two blocks that are never combined: (1) companyDeals: power contracts of the five covered companies, from their filings (T1) or their own / their counterparty's announcements (T2: company statement, not audited; a counterparty's 8-K exhibit is still the counterparty's statement); (2) grid: national and regional projections and measurements from regulators and grid operators (T3: EIA, NERC, ERCOT, PJM) and third-party estimates (T4: LBNL, IEA). MW in a contract are nameplate or contract quantity as the announcement states; they are not data center IT load and are never read as data center IT load. Staleness: T1 next filing + 7 days; T3/T4 publisher's next edition + 30 days (nextExpected). source_type nuclear_uprate: capacity added by reactor uprates. press: dated press notes (T3) attached to a deal (gas supply, delays), shown apart and entering no figure. grid kind 'rule': a regulator's or grid operator's rule with its status, not a projection. page_es: the Spanish wording of the page/section citation.

grid.context_es: El consejo de PJM instruyó el 27 jul 2026 un «Servicio Interino de Adecuación de Recursos»: las grandes cargas nuevas que no aportaran generación propia a partir del 1 jun 2027 serían las primeras en recortarse en una escasez. La FERC rechazó esa parte (y el esquema «trae tu propia capacidad nueva») en su orden del 9 oct 2026 y aceptó solo la definición de gran carga y el registro; PJM debe presentar lenguaje tarifario revisado en 30 días. Mientras no haya una nueva orden, no rige ningún recorte prioritario a las cargas nuevas.
grid.context_en: PJM's Board directed on 27 Jul 2026 an "Interim Resource Adequacy Service": new large loads that did not bring their own generation from 1 Jun 2027 would be curtailed first in a shortage. FERC rejected that part (and the "bring your own new capacity" option) in its order of 9 Oct 2026 and accepted only the large-load definition and the registry; PJM must file revised tariff language within 30 days. Until a new order, no curtail-first rule applies to new loads.
